name: Antitrust Procedure Regulation
evidence_rating: thin: Commission evaluations based on enforcement records, consultation and a support study; no independent study of the Regulation's effect on enforcement outcomes
summary: Regulation 1/2003 ended the notification of agreements to the Commission and shared enforcement with national authorities and courts. The Commission's 2024 evaluation judged the framework broadly effective, citing 225 Commission enforcement decisions and more than EUR 42 billion in fines over 20 years, but found procedures slow and less suited to digital markets; a revision is under way.

indicators.objective: No monitoring indicators set in the proposal; assessed through the Commission's reports listed below
Effective and uniform enforcement of Articles 101 and 102
indicators.evidence: 2004-2024: 225 Commission enforcement decisions; fines above EUR 42 billion (about EUR 37 billion upheld by the EU Courts).

literature.citation: European Commission (2024), Evaluation of Regulations 1/2003 and 773/2004 (antitrust enforcement framework), SWD(2024) 217
literature.title: Evaluation of Regulations 1/2003 and 773/2004 (antitrust enforcement framework)
literature.method: ex-post evaluation (public consultation, workshop, external support study)
literature.headline: Framework broadly met its goal of effective, efficient and uniform application of EU competition rules; 225 enforcement decisions and over EUR 42 billion in fines in 20 years; procedures seen as slow, notably for digital markets
literature.summary_plain: The Commission found the decentralised antitrust system it created in 2004 works, but that cases take long, which led to a planned revision.

literature.citation: European Commission (2009), Report on the functioning of Regulation 1/2003, COM(2009) 206
literature.title: Report on the functioning of Regulation 1/2003
literature.outcomes: enforcement; cooperation in the competition network
literature.headline: Five years on, the Regulation had transformed enforcement: more cases by national authorities, cooperation through the European Competition Network, and an end to notifications
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's first review found the 2004 reform had made antitrust enforcement across the EU more active and better coordinated.
